question: A doctor prescribes metformin 500 mg twice daily to a newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patient and says only: 'Take two tablets a day, one after breakfast and one after dinner.' According to the WHO five-element drug counselling framework, which element is MOST clearly omitted?

answers.text: How to take the medicine (route and timing)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The doctor has explained when to take the tablets (after breakfast and dinner). This element is adequately covered in the instruction given.

answers.text: Why the medicine is being prescribed (indication and therapeutic goal)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WHO framework requires: (1) why — indication and expected benefit, (2) how — dose, route, timing, (3) what to expect — effects and side effects, (4) what to do if problems occur, (5) how to store. The instruction given covers 'how' but entirely omits 'why' — the patient does not know they have diabetes or what the drug aims to achieve.

answers.text: What side effects may occur and how to manage them

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Side effect counselling is important but is not the MOST critically omitted element. Without understanding why the drug is being prescribed, patients lack the context to value adherence at all.
Storage counselling is part of the framework but is the least critical omission here. The far more consequential gap is the patient's lack of understanding of their diagnosis and treatment goal.

overallFeedback.feedback: Apply the WHO five-element framework: why, how, what to expect, what to do if problems arise, storage. The instruction given only addresses 'how'. 'Why' — the diagnosis and therapeutic objective — is the most critically missing element.
Correct. 'Why' — conveying the diagnosis, the treatment goal, and the expected benefit — is the foundational element. Without it, patients cannot make an informed choice to adhere.
